note: New page: no old Notion text of its own. This maps every fact about memory in the old hardware root and its four old children (saved verbatim by the root in ../../src/read/old/) to where this page carries it, or why not. Checked 2026-10-05.

facts.claim: HBM stacked beside the GPU on an interposer, 1,024-bit per stack; H100 3.35, H200 4.8, B200 8 TB/s; Rubin HBM4 '~13 TB/s class'
facts.evidence: Rubin is 22 TB/s on NVIDIA's Rubin blog and HGX page, 19.2 TB/s on the Vera Rubin NVL72 page (both shown); the rest verified; HBM4 interface 2,048 bits (Rambus)

facts.claim: RTX 5090 GDDR7 on a 512-bit bus, 1.79 TB/s, 32 GB
facts.evidence: RTX Blackwell whitepaper
facts.where: Reading s4, in-one-screen table, width x rate chart

facts.claim: GDDR7 has 'no ECC by default'
facts.evidence: not in the whitepaper; Micron lists on-die ECC for its GDDR7 devices, which is not the same as end-to-end ECC; not stated on the page

facts.claim: 'while one warp waits ~400 cycles on a DRAM load'
facts.evidence: Luo et al. Table IV measure 466 to 542 cycles of global-memory latency on A100, H800, RTX 4090; this page measures about 467 ns on the M1 Pro GPU

facts.claim: register file 256 KB, L1/shared up to 228 KB per SM (Hopper), 50 MB L2
facts.evidence: CUDA Programming Guide tables (via the shared facts file); used for the 119 MB on-chip total

facts.claim: Groq LPU: no HBM, ~230 MB SRAM per chip
facts.evidence: Groq's current page lists the announced Groq 3 LPX rack: 256 LPUs, 128 GB SRAM, 40 PB/s (0.5 GB per chip derived); first-generation 230 MB not verified

facts.claim: Cerebras WSE-3 44 GB on-chip SRAM
facts.evidence: Cerebras press release Mar 13 2024 (21 PB/s)

facts.claim: moving a byte from DRAM costs orders of magnitude more energy than a MAC
facts.evidence: Horowitz 45 nm table via Han et al. 2015: 640 pJ per 32-bit DRAM read against 3.7 pJ per 32-bit float multiply (173x); HBM2 3.92 pJ/bit (O'Connor et al. 2017)

facts.claim: Unified Buffer / CMEM / VMEM software-managed SRAM
facts.evidence: TPUs and other accelerators

facts.claim: Ironwood 192 GB HBM3e, 7.4 TB/s
facts.evidence: TPU7x docs: 192 GiB, 7,380 GB/s (the shared facts file)

facts.claim: MI400 432 GB HBM4; Helios rack 31 TB
facts.evidence: AMD MI400 page via the shared facts file: 432 GB HBM4, 23.3 TB/s

facts.claim: KV per token = 2 x L x n_kv x d_head x bytes; Llama 3.1 8B 128 KB/token; 8K tokens about 1 GB
facts.evidence: computed from config.json: 131,072 B; 8,192 tokens = 1.07 GB

facts.claim: 64K context with FP8 KV: '64K x 128 KB / 8'
facts.evidence: FP8 halves BF16 (divide by 2, not 8); this page says FP8 halves the cache

facts.claim: why serving quantises KV to FP8 and why GQA exists
facts.evidence: GQA, MQA, MLA, sliding windows and hybrid linear layers compared on 13 real configs

facts.claim: decode ceiling = bandwidth / (weight bytes + KV bytes per token)
facts.evidence: measured on the M1 Pro: decode attention time follows cache bytes for GQA (141 GB/s fit)
facts.where: Reading s6, Memory lab 3, KV tab planner

facts.claim: 8B full fine-tune (128 GB) does not fit two 5090s without ZeRO-offload; 70B states 1.1 TB > 640 GB, offload or more nodes
facts.evidence: offload transfer times derived for PCIe Gen5, NVLink-C2C and the measured SSD; ZeRO-Infinity

facts.claim: bandwidth hierarchy: HBM 3.35 to 8 TB/s, NVLink 900 GB/s / 1.8 TB/s, IB 50 to 100 GB/s per NIC, storage Ethernet ~10 GB/s
facts.evidence: storage tier replaced by this laptop's measured SSD; directions made explicit

facts.claim: DRAM prices up ~500% in twelve months, 128 GB DDR5 $3,399 (Tom's Hardware)
facts.evidence: secondary source only

facts.claim: Samsung expected to more than double HBM4 and HBM4E output in 2027
facts.evidence: no primary source found

facts.claim: High-bandwidth flash (HBF) at Hot Chips 2026
facts.evidence: no primary source found

facts.claim: Positron Asimov, commodity-memory bet
facts.evidence: secondary source only; the idea (capacity against bandwidth) is s5

facts.claim: Memory technology: HBM generations, packaging, GDDR, CXL and memory tiers
facts.evidence: HBM generations, packaging, GDDR, LPDDR, tiers and offload covered; CXL not covered (no primary source fetched in this build; a candidate for a later pass)
